A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Sherlock and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–E. Retained content can be matched reliably despite pagination changes and additions to Appendix D.

before.justification: v1 reports original self-correction experiments, eight-benchmark evaluations of Sherlock, training-objective ablations, and inference-efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds training-time comparisons, initialization experiments, and an evaluated LLaVA-Reasoner-DPO baseline in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a limited application variant: directly apply Sherlock's offline preference stage to an already-trained LLaVA-CoT model, bypassing cold-start. The principal three-stage algorithm, losses, visual perturbation construction, and dynamic beta remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Sherlock retains the LLaVA-CoT training source and the same eight evaluation benchmarks and task domains. Appendix D adds comparisons and initialization variants without establishing new dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 8 newly evaluates LLaVA-Reasoner-DPO against Sherlock under direct generation and self-correction. Its underlying work was already cited in v1, but it was not an evaluated comparator. Existing comparator sets in Tables 1–5 are retained.

E3.justification: Appendix D introduces LLaVA-CoT initialization experiments using cold-start or direct offline training. The new DPO comparison specifies the shared Llama3.2-Vision-11B-Instruct backbone and a 258k annotated-data budget. Existing benchmark splits, metrics, and three-round self-correction evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 7 adds an initialization study testing whether Sherlock's training stages improve an existing reasoning model, and Table 7 adds a training-efficiency comparison. Earlier loss and dynamic-beta ablations, correction-turn analysis, and four case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version provides repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new experiments retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main results remain unchanged, including Sherlock Iter2's 64.1 direct and 65.4 self-corrected averages. New results include LLaVA-Reasoner-DPO's 60.6/59.0 averages in Table 8 and LLaVA-CoT cold-start's 62.8/63.2 and offline training's 63.6/64.2 in Figure 7. Table 7 adds training-time values of 160, 288, and 128 for LLaVA-CoT, LlamaV-o1, and Sherlock, without specifying units.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, definitions, and Appendix A derivation are unchanged apart from citation numbering and formatting. No new theorem, assumption, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about trajectory-level self-correction, self-improvement with 20k annotations, and reasoning and inference-efficiency benefits. Headline performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix D newly attributes possible overfitting and limited correction gains to reusing data already seen by LLaVA-CoT, and attributes training efficiency to data efficiency and an RL-free design. Its claim that LLaVA-Reasoner-DPO fails to improve through CoT training overstates Table 8, where direct accuracy averages 60.6 versus the base model's 58.7.

D1.justification: v2 specifies VL-Rethinker-7B in Table 1 and replaces the SFT alpha and beta-DPO values with dashes in Table 6, consistent with the unchanged SFT objective. It adds training-time figures but removes v1's explicit LLaMA-Factory and eight-A100 training disclosure. Table 7 leaves timing units and measurement conditions unspecified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Rong et al.'s backdoor-cleaning paper as a citation for visual perturbation and removes the LLaMA-Factory reference. Appendix D adds substantive comparison with the already-cited LLaVA-Reasoner-DPO work; the main related-work positioning otherwise remains stable.

P1.justification: Several paragraphs in Sections 3–5 are condensed or rewritten, the main training setup is shortened, acknowledgements are added, and Appendix D is renamed and subdivided. The overall narrative and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–8 and Figure 7, relocates the retained Figure 6 within the expanded appendix, and reflows main-text material including Table 5. Existing figure designs, table structures, and case-study displays are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: Appendix D fills two useful evaluation gaps: comparison with another DPO-based reasoning approach and application to an already-trained reasoning model. These additions modestly strengthen empirical support. The gain is limited by removed training software/hardware disclosure, unspecified timing units, and an interpretation of the DPO results that overstates Table 8.
